newsitem.title: USA: U.S. plays down Iraq report on spy network.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plays down Iraq report on spy network.

text.p: A U.S. official said on Friday a report that Iraq uncovered a CIA spy network might be a "propaganda ploy" to show Saddam Hussein's son Uday was still in control after an assassination attempt.
The Central Intelligence Agency declined comment on Iraq's claim that it had uncovered a network of confessed CIA spies.
In Baghdad, the Iraqi News Agency said members of the group admitted they carried out spying activities in Iraq.
"Baghdad television said members of the group have confessed their activities against Iraq, its people and its leader President Saddam Hussein," INA said.
The agency said the state-run television and Youth television, owned by Saddam's eldest son Uday, would interview the group at 10 p.m. local (1900 GMT).
But a U.S. official called the report a possible "propaganda ploy" aimed at showing Uday Hussein was in control after surviving an apparent assassination attempt last week.
"I don't think that this is a new development," the official said.

He said any Iraqis about to be put on display as alleged CIA agents could include some of those detained by Saddam in early September after Iraqi forces drove into a Western-protected Kurdish safe haven in Northern Iraq.
The official added that when the Iraqis capture suspected spies they typically "grill them" for months.

According to Iraqi dissident groups, when the Iraqi forces marched into the Kurdish enclave, they broke up a long-standing CIA-funded covert operation to destabilize Saddam Hussein. More than 100 Iraqis were arrested and executed and others were taken prisoner, according to the dissident groups.
In September, the movement of Iraqi troops into the Kurdish enclave sparked renewed tension with the United States.
To punish Saddam at the time, the United States launched cruise missiles against Iraqi air defenses and expanded the no-fly zone in Iraq.
